transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-12
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Sam (OrionEdge SRE), Maya (Head of Infra), Liam (Platform Eng), Rina (Security)

Summary:
- Quick recap of last week's outage (inference nodes experienced cascade of memory pressure tied to K-V cache growth).
- Root cause hypothesis validated: cache fill + incorrect TTL eviction under a malformed prefix leading to OOM and degraded tail latency.
- Discussed mitigation plan: immediate config change, medium-term patch to eviction logic, long-term runbook & SLA changes.

Topics covered:
- Root cause walkthrough
- Patch vs config tradeoffs
- Rollout timeline and maintenance window
- Audit, logs and evidence for customer SOC/compliance team
- Risk transfer: how Redwood will own rollback and on-call support during rollout

Action items (recap included above).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Alright, thanks everyone for making time. We're gonna run a quick debrief and handoff for the stability work. I think we have a fairly tight agenda, um, we wanna make sure the RCA is clear and the rollback plan is owned.
[00:28] Sam (SRE): Yep, thanks. Just so you know, we had two short P99 spikes then the pod restart storm. We saw KV cache grow, there was a key prefix from a new feature that didn't set a TTL.
[00:45] Priya (SE): Right, and from the traces we looked at the Gpu worker's memory footprint rose linearly until it hit the soft OOM, and that caused thrashing. The continuous batcher held onto the KV references, so they weren't freed.
[01:12] Maya (Head of Infra): One thing, the telemetry looked different across regions — eu-west had more aggressive rate limits, but the root pattern is the same. We need to be sure regional config diff wasn't a contributing factor.
[01:34] Liam (Platform Eng): Also, we noticed a correlation with the canary deploy that introduced the new prefix. Timeline-wise it's basically aligned.
[01:50] Alex (AE): Good call. Priya, we validated the hypothesis with the live heap snapshots?
[01:56] Priya (SE): Yeah we pulled two heap diffs from the affected pods. There's a high churn of small KV entries tied to the feature's session token handling — looks like values were small but unbounded. Memory pressure, then eviction didn't kick because the TTL was never set. Also a few mis-typed config keys — sometimes the agent reads "K V cache" in logs which complicates parsers.
[02:28] Rina (Security): From the security lens, we need the audit trail for all config changes and the redwood side mutation logs. SOC2 team will want timestamps and operator IDs. Can you confirm you have immutable logs?
[02:45] Jordan (CSM): Yes, we can provide the audit exports. Redwood's control plane records the config change events and we can share the signed export. We'll redact anything PII.
[03:05] Sam (SRE): Great. We're mostly worried about two things: 1) risk of a bad patch making things worse during high traffic, and 2) the potential for a rollback to not clean up leaked KV entries so we get recurrent pressure.
[03:30] Priya (SE): For 1) we propose a staged rollout: change default TTL to 1h for the affected prefix via remote config first, monitor for 24 hours, then release a code patch that enforces TTLs at the writer. For 2) the patch will include a garbage collection pass that can be run as a maintenance job to evict leaked keys older than X.
[04:02] Maya (Head of Infra): What's the expected downtime or impact during the GC pass?
[04:09] Priya (SE): The GC job is read-only from the serving plane's perspective; it will clean up entries via a background sweep that throttles concurrency. We don't expect downtime but there will be additional CPU/IO on the KV nodes — we recommend running it outside peak, hence the maintenance window ask.
[04:34] Liam (Platform Eng): If the GC doesn't finish before peak, can we pause it? What's the safe pause/resume semantics?
[04:42] Priya (SE): Yes, it's pausable. We expose a controller endpoint to pause and resume, and it also checkpoints progress.
[04:55] Sam (SRE): Ok that helps. Second question: how do we validate that the same bad prefix won't be reintroduced from application deploys?
[05:05] Alex (AE): There's an ops-level quarantine we can add — a lint in the SDK and a pre-deploy check that rejects writes without TTL for certain prefixes. We can also push a runtime guard that rejects writes with missing TTL and returns a 4xx instead of silently accepting.
[05:28] Rina (Security): The runtime guard returning 4xx concerns product teams; we need to ensure it doesn't lead to downstream errors. We might prefer a circuit-breaker that logs and drops, with an alert to the deploy owner.
[05:45] Jordan (CSM): We'll draft both options and align with your dev leads.
[06:00] [silence, keyboard clatter]
[06:15] Priya (SE): On the rollback semantics — if we need to rollback to previous runtime behavior, we must also back out the GC or at least have a replay mechanism to restore keys if the app expects them. The GC will archive keys for 7 days before permanent deletion so we can restore if needed.
[06:42] Sam (SRE): Archive location? On our side or Redwood?
[06:46] Priya (SE): Redwood will store the archive in a customer-isolated bucket in your VPC when on Private. For hosted we provide encrypted archive in our storage with S3-compatible signed export. Rina, that's part of the compliance package.
[07:05] Rina (Security): We need to validate key ownership and encryption (KMS). Can you confirm whether the archive is encrypted with a customer-managed key?
[07:18] Priya (SE): For Private deployments yes, you can bring your own KMS. For hosted we offer CMK integration for enterprise tier — we can negotiate per contract.
[07:34] Maya (Head of Infra): Timeline — we need the short-term config flip as soon as possible. What minimal steps does Redwood need to perform and what do we need to sign off?
[07:45] Alex (AE): Minimal steps: Redwood will push remote-config default TTL for the prefix, monitor for 24 hours, and then schedule GC + patch. We need your approval for the maintenance window and for read-only archive access.
[08:02] Liam (Platform Eng): How long is the maintenance window?
[08:06] Priya (SE): We suggest a 3-hour window in the 02:00-05:00 UTC night window to run the GC and canary the patch on 5% traffic for 30 minutes then ramp to 25% then 100% if metrics look good.
[08:26] Sam (SRE): Sounds reasonable. What rollback criteria do we have?
[08:30] Priya (SE): If P99 latency increases by more than 20% from baseline, or error rate (5xx from the runtime guard) exceeds 1% over 5 minutes, we auto-roll back. We'll keep a manual override for you.
[08:47] Alex (AE): We'll also include an ops-runbook with run commands for pause/resume, manual key restore, and checklist items.
[09:00] Rina (Security): On audit items — please include signed mutation logs, TLS cert rotation proof, and KMS key IDs. Also provide a retention policy for the GC archives.
[09:18] Jordan (CSM): Noted. We'll assemble the artifacts and share a link to the secure bucket.
[09:25] [short cross-talk]
[09:40] Sam (SRE): One more ask — can Redwood take on paging for the initial rollout night? We want Redwood engineers at-hand to own rollback if needed.
[09:50] Alex (AE): Yes, Redwood will provide on-call coverage for the rollout window and will be primary for rollback execution. We can add the shift to the incident rotation for that night.
[10:05] Maya (Head of Infra): Costs — will there be any incremental charges for the GC job or archive storage?
[10:12] Alex (AE): There will be modest storage fees for archives during the 7-day retention; we'll provide an estimate. No extra charges for the maintenance window itself for the first emergency mitigation — we'll treat it as part of the incident SLA.
[10:30] Priya (SE): Quick technical note: the GC will be implemented as a consistent scanner using cursor-based pagination to avoid hotspotting. It uses our internal backpressure signals so it plays nice with normal traffic.
[10:50] Liam (Platform Eng): Ok. For the pre-deploy check — what's the integration effort? We run CI with a lint job; can you provide a plugin?
[10:58] Priya (SE): Yes, small SDK change plus a static lint rule. We can provide a simple GitHub Action and the plugin in a PR format.
[11:10] Jordan (CSM): Next steps recap — Alex will share traces and RCA by Tues 03-14, Priya will share patch plan by 03-18, customer to pick a maintenance window (target 03-20), and we'll schedule a dry-run week of 03-26.
[11:35] Sam (SRE): Fine. Also we may want to run a chaos exercise afterwards to validate the runbook.
[11:45] Alex (AE): Agreed, we'll schedule a small blast radius test in a staging environment first.
[11:55] Priya (SE): Any other open concerns?
[12:00] Rina (Security): Please include legal on the archive retention terms; we need to be clear if Redwood can access archives for hosted customers.
[12:08] Alex (AE): We'll include that in the artifacts.
[12:15] [meeting wrap, thanks]

References shared during call:
- RCA draft (link to be shared)

End of transcript.
